notes: Strong wind/solar pipeline. ERCOT permitting is fastest in the country. Grid isolation is a reliability risk (2021 event). Water stress in western TX; Dallas-Fort Worth less constrained. PPA market is the most active in the US.

Largest data center market in the world (Ashburn / Prince William). Demand ceiling is high but buildable land is nearly exhausted. PJM interconnection queue is severely backlogged. Virginia VCEA mandates 100% clean electricity by 2050. Renewable colocation potential within VA is limited — requires out-of-state sourcing.

Emerging hub anchored by AWS Columbus and Meta New Albany campuses. PJM queue backlog is improving in Ohio but still significant. Ohio RPS is weak (~8.5%), limiting clean energy policy tailwind. Great Lakes region provides strong water availability.

Iowa has the highest wind capacity factors in CONUS. Google has operated data centers here since 2007. Wholesale prices are among the cheapest in the dataset. Limited tech talent base constrains demand-side growth. Strong co-location potential for wind-coupled AI campuses.

Highest wind capacity factors in the dataset. Near-zero hyperscale presence today makes this a greenfield opportunity rather than a near-term demand story. Lowest land costs and fast interconnection. Western Kansas faces moderate water stress. Underpenetrated by corporate PPA buyers.

Strongest policy environment and deepest PPA market in the US. Highest wholesale power prices, most constrained interconnection queue, highest land costs, and water scarcity make new greenfield development extremely challenging. Included as a demand-rich / supply-constrained reference case.

Hydro-dominant grid provides cheap, reliable, clean baseload power. Microsoft and Amazon are headquartered here. Clean energy penetration is highest in the dataset. Water availability is excellent. Columbia River basin hydro faces long-run climate risk (lower snowpack projections). Strong policy environment.

Georgia Power (Southern Company) provides reliable, low-cost regulated utility service. Microsoft and Google have announced major data center investments in metro Atlanta. Nuclear baseload (Plant Vogtle) provides clean firm power. Clean energy penetration is low overall. Business-friendly permitting environment.
